message.reasoning:
This is a MitM tool-traffic redirect finding. Entry point: network access to MCP port 7013. Not natural language control really — LC: the attacker supplies JSON-RPC tool call, attacker controls tool name/args. LC probably D (attacker-supplied input reaches privileged tool path). Actually the documented attack is a redirect on the proxy path — not language-mediated. The implemented default: transfer_funds returns scripted result to whatever destination caller names. It's a network attack, no NL. LC could be N (no natural language path to security-relevant behaviour)? But the tool call arguments are attacker-controlled... The rubric LC: "attacker-supplied natural language reaches a privileged decision or tool-invocation path." JSON-RPC args are structured, not NL. But entry point as implemented is attacker-supplied tool calls directly. Hmm. I'd say D direct — attacker supplies tool call that reaches tool invocation without mediation (ProxyBot accepts any tool name, no auth). I'll go D.

CP: N (stateless). AP: effect on ProxyBot component only — contained within one component? The documented attack redirects traffic to attacker endpoint — crossing trust boundary (attacker's endpoint). AP C (relays across agent components... ) or L? Traffic rerouted to attacker's endpoint = crossing trust boundary into another principal? The impact is on downstream/attacker. I'd say L lateral (crossing into attacker's domain) — but actually the attack is MitM; compromised traffic flows to attacker. I'll pick C: contained, since it stays within ProxyBot's principal domain... Hmm. The redirect sends fund-transfer data to attacker's endpoint — that crosses a trust boundary. AP L.

RH: no evaluator/reward channel — N? No test confirms isolation. RH X or N. There's no proxy objective at all; the agent just executes tool calls. RH N requires a test confirming isolation. No such test. I'll say X? Rubric: N requires every evaluator outside reach and test confirms isolation. No evidence of any evaluator, so "the agent can reach a proxy objective... and no verified episode" — can't reach one either. I'll go N? Risky. Pick X with low confidence? RH N seems safer since no evaluator exists in the lab at all for ProxyBot... but N demands a test. I'll go X, verified_episodes 0, reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified false.

ES: ProxyBot accepts any tool name, dynamic resolution with no constraints — W wide.

CVSS: network (Docker 0.0.0.0 but published on loopback; default binds 127.0.0.1 — local? Attacker needs network access to MCP port; default localhost → AV:L). Actually documented attack needs MITM on path to tools; as implemented entry via JSON-RPC to 7013, bound 127.0.0.1 default. AV:L, AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N, VC:H? transfer_funds reported as done — simulated only, no real funds. Impact: spoofed transaction success — integrity of the vulnerable system (fake financial record). VC:N/VI:L? Data is simulated. VI:L (false transfer record). VA:N. Downstream: attacker receives traffic — SC:N, SI:N/ SA:N? As documented, tool traffic rerouted through attacker endpoint — confidentiality of tool calls exposed → SC:L? Hmm as implemented, no redirect followed. Score as-implemented: attacker can call transfer_funds directly and get "done" — that's the vulnerability itself, spoofing result. VI:L on the agent app. Let's give vector: AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N. Keep simple.

AIVSS: LC=D, CP=N, AP=C, RH=X, ES=W.

automatable: Yes (automated test exists).

technical_impact: Partial (simulated transfer, no real funds).

applicability: model_directed_goal_pursuit false in both — no model in default. As modeled also scripted.
